title: Freedom, Knowledge and Caring for Others
overview: Paul answers a question about eating meat offered to idols by arguing that love for fellow believers should shape how people use their freedom.

parts.label: Knowledge versus love (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: In Corinth, meat from animals sacrificed at temples was eaten at feasts there or sold in the market, and the church had asked Paul whether believers could eat it. Paul seems to echo their own claim that they all had the right knowledge, then answers that knowledge alone can make people proud, while love builds others up and being known by God matters most.

parts.label: One God, one Lord (vv. 4-6)
parts.note: Paul agrees that idols are not real gods, even though people around them honored many gods and lords. He restates the Jewish belief in one God and names Jesus as the one Lord through whom all things exist, a line Christians read as a very early statement that Jesus shares God's identity.

parts.label: Not everyone feels free (vv. 7-8)
parts.note: Some believers had worshiped idols all their lives and still felt the meat belonged to the god, so eating it left them feeling guilty and stained. Paul adds that food itself does not change anyone's standing with God, whether they eat or not.

parts.label: Freedom that harms (vv. 9-12)
parts.note: A confident believer seen eating at a temple feast might lead an uneasy believer to copy them against their own conscience, tripping them up in their faith. Paul says this can ruin that person, and that wounding someone Christ died for is a wrong against Christ himself.

parts.label: Paul's own choice (v. 13)
parts.note: Paul says he would give up meat completely rather than cause a fellow believer to fall. He returns to the subject of idol food in chapter 10.

disagreement: Christians differ on how far this principle reaches, especially whether the weak means only people who might actually be led into wrongdoing or anyone who disapproves, and so how much one person's freedom should give way to another's scruples.
think: Have you ever been right about something but found that being right mattered less than how your actions affected someone else?
